sections.heading: A Metal Roof Is a Bigger Question Than Shingles
body: You have seen metal on barns, churches and the shop down the road. On a house it is a different decision, and the quote in your hand may not say much: which kind of panel, which finish, and what the roof sits on.
A roofer that specializes in metal can answer those questions. That is the work Pioneer Roofing does.

sections.heading: Metal Roofing Services in Peoria
sections.intro: Metal roofing comes first, for homes and for commercial buildings. Repairs follow.

sections.heading: Which Metal Roof Fits Which Building
body: Metal roofing is not one product. These are the kinds you will hear about, in plain words, so you know what to ask for.

items.title: Standing seam
items.text: Long panels joined at raised seams, with the fasteners usually hidden underneath. The surface stays smooth.

items.title: Corrugated
items.text: Panels with a wavy profile, the look most people picture on barns and outbuildings. The fasteners usually go through the face of the panel.

items.title: Metal shingles
items.text: Smaller pieces of metal made to resemble shingles, shake or slate, for a house that should still look like a house.

items.title: Commercial metal roofing
items.text: A larger building brings different questions: drainage, access to the roof and how the space underneath is used.

sections.quote: Great people to do business with very fair and transparent
sections.name: Marty B.

sections.heading: Homes and Commercial Buildings Want Different Things
body: A house has valleys, a chimney and a ridge to work around, and the roof is part of how the house looks from the street.
A commercial building is usually larger and simpler in shape, so drainage and access matter more than curb appeal. We install metal roofs on both.
Either way, the choice of roof should start from the building, not from a catalog.

sections.heading: What a Metal Roof Quote Should Spell Out
body: A good quote names the kind of panel, says how it is fastened and describes the details at the edges, valleys and vents. If any of that is missing, ask. The [metal roofing page](/metal-roofing-peoria-il/) lists the five questions worth asking any roofer, us included.

sections.heading: Standing Seam, Corrugated and Metal Shingles
body: The names get used loosely, so here is what each one means.

items.title: Standing seam
items.text: Long panels that run along the roof and join at raised seams. The fasteners are usually hidden beneath the seams, so the roof surface is smooth with no screw heads showing.

items.title: Corrugated
items.text: Panels with a wavy profile, which is the look most people picture on a barn or a shed, usually fastened through the face of the panel.

items.title: Metal shingles
items.text: Small pieces of metal made to resemble shingles, shake or slate. They are for people who want a metal roof that does not look like a barn.

sections.heading: Choosing a Metal Roof for a House
body: For a house, the roof is part of how the home looks from the street, so the decision is partly about appearance. The panel type, the color and the trim along the edges all show.
It is also about the roof's shape. A simple gable takes metal differently than a roof with valleys, dormers and a chimney, and the details at those spots decide how the roof sheds water.

sections.quote: This company is definitely determine get the job done
sections.name: Ernest R.

sections.heading: Where a Metal Roof Is Won or Lost: Edges, Valleys and Vents
body: Water gets into any roof where the roof changes direction or something passes through it. On metal, that means the trim at the edges, the valleys, the vents and the chimney.
Metal also expands and contracts with the temperature. A good installation allows for that, which is one more reason to ask how the trim is made and fastened.

sections.heading: Commercial Metal Roofing
body: A commercial building is usually bigger and simpler in shape than a house, so the questions change. How does water leave the roof? How do people get up there for service? What is going on underneath?
Pioneer Roofing installs commercial metal roofs as well as residential ones.

sections.heading: Questions to Ask Before You Sign for a Metal Roof
body: A metal roof quote can leave out parts that matter. Ask any roofer, including us, these five things.

items.title: Which panel is it, and why?
items.text: The answer should name the type and tie it to your roof, not just say metal.

items.title: How is it fastened?
items.text: Hidden fasteners and exposed fasteners age differently.

items.title: What goes underneath?
items.text: The layer under the metal matters as much as the metal.

items.title: How are the details handled?
items.text: Edges, valleys, vents and chimneys are where leaks start.

items.title: Who stands behind it?
items.text: Get what the roofer covers and what the manufacturer covers in writing.

sections.heading: Repairs and Solar
body: A metal roof that already exists can need work too, and we handle repairs. If you are thinking about solar panels on the roof, mention it when you call so it is part of the conversation from the start.

sections.heading: Questions About Metal Roofing in Peoria

items.q: How is a metal roof different from a shingle roof?
items.a: A shingle roof is many small pieces laid in overlapping rows. A metal roof is long panels or larger pieces fastened to the roof, with the joints and trim doing the work of keeping water out.

items.q: Do you install metal roofs on commercial buildings?
items.a: Yes, along with residential metal roofs.

items.q: What does a metal roof cost?
items.a: It depends on the building, the kind of panel and the shape of the roof, so we do not name a number sight unseen. Call (309) 865-5471 and ask.

items.q: Can you do standing seam and corrugated?
items.a: Yes. Both are part of our metal roofing work.

footer.about: Pioneer Roofing is a metal roofing company at 202 SW Center St in Peoria, IL. It installs residential and commercial metal roofs and handles repairs, for Peoria and nearby towns.

why: Your site has real metal roofing pages for homes, commercial buildings, standing seam, corrugated and installation and design. Their headlines say METAL ROOFS and STANDING SEAM METAL ROOFS with no city, so someone searching for a metal roof in Peoria has nothing built for that phrase.

At least 36 town pages each say "Pioneer Roofing Experts in" a town, and they are one page with the town name swapped, so Google reads the same words again and again. The Phone button on every one we checked dials (321) 399-2147, not the (309) 865-5471 printed everywhere else.
So we built a site around the work you are known for: metal roofing in Peoria on a page of its own, the towns you serve on the homepage, and one phone number.
